Hi Daniel —

Following up on the technical items Marissa outlined. Key points up front: Redwood supports three private deployment packaging modes and an air‑gapped workflow. Details below and I've attached an architecture diagram and an installer matrix.

1) Packaging / Installer options
- Containerized bundle (recommended): a tarball of signed container images + manifest that can be loaded into a local registry. Supports Kubernetes distributions (EKS‑D, AKS‑D, OpenShift, upstream K8s).
- OVA/VM image: for customers that prefer VM appliance. Includes preconfigured systemd services and the runtime.
- Bare‑metal installation: for tightly controlled environments; we provide an installer binary and orchestration playbooks.

Lead times:
- Standard container bundle: ~2–3 business days after contract and sizing signoff.
- OVA / custom images: ~7–14 business days depending on QA and OS hardening requirements.
- Fully custom bare‑metal: timeline varies; typically 2–4 weeks for validation.

2) Air‑gapped specifics
- Offline image transfer: we provide signed image artifacts + SHA256 checksums and PGP signatures. Customer loads to local registry; no outbound network required once images are staged.
- Local dependency registry: installer can be configured to point to an internal registry and local artifact store.
- Upgrade: patch bundles are delivered as signed artifacts; upgrades can be applied offline.

3) KMS / HSM
- Supported: AWS KMS (via VPC endpoints), Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS (if required), and customer‑managed HSMs that expose PKCS#11.
- We support key import and HSM‑backed signing for LLM model keys and encryption keys. For air‑gapped deployments, HSM appliance can be used on‑prem without outbound dependencies.

4) Network & ports
- Base requirements are documented in the attached diagram. For air‑gapped mode we allow a zero‑egress profile. If telemetry is desired, it is toggled explicitly and only uses configured egress endpoints.

Attachments: private_deploy_arch.png, installer_matrix.pdf

If you share your preferred K8s distro and node sizing, I can produce a tailored manifest and exact image sizes. Happy to walk through specifics on the call with Marissa.

—Jasmine
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Daniel / Priya —

Attaching the security artifacts you requested and a completed version of the questionnaire. Highlights below; the attached PDF contains line‑by‑line answers mapped to your spreadsheet.

- SOC 2 Type II: latest report attached (SOC2_Report_Q4_2025.pdf) covering our control environment for hosted and private offerings when operated under Redwood managed services. For on‑prem deployments, the control ownership model is captured in the questionnaire; Redwood provides configuration guidance and audit hooks but the customer retains responsibility for physical infrastructure controls.
- Telemetry & telemetry in air‑gapped mode: When air‑gapped mode is selected, the runtime disables outbound telemetry by default. We can provide an attestation of zero telemetry collection in that mode and a minimal local audit log that stays on‑prem.
- Encryption: All customer data at rest is encrypted with AES‑GCM using keys that can be managed by customer KMS/HSM. In transit, we enforce TLS1.3 between components.
- Audit & logging: Detailed audit logs (request IDs, model version, token counts) are available via local log collectors and can be forwarded to customer SIEMs; for air‑gapped installs forwarding is disabled by default.
- Key rotation: We support automated rotation with customer KMS APIs or manual rotation workflows when using an HSM.
- Vulnerability management: CVE response SLAs and patch cadence are in the attached questionnaire.

Attachments: PrivDeploy_Security_Questionnaire_Filled.pdf, SOC2_Report_Q4_2025.pdf

If Acme legal needs a formal attestation letter or a redlineable SLA appendix for private deployment, loop in Laura and we'll produce a tailored MOA/SLA addendum.

—Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security Compliance
Redwood Inference
